pinned.input_coercion: booleans unchanged; strings true/1/yes/pinned after str(...).strip().lower() -> true; other strings -> false; other types -> bool(value)

size_bytes.input_coercion: int(str(size_bytes).strip()); on failure int(float(str(size_bytes).strip())); on failure 0

ts.input_coercion: int(str(ts).strip()); on failure int(float(str(ts).strip())); on failure 0

inventory_source.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline; each record carries its fields in the order the source lists them -- snapshot_id, repo, vault, ts, size_bytes, pinned, note -- and the key sorting the two report objects use does not apply here

retention_decisions_jsonl.container: one compact JSON object per line, json.dumps(..., separators=(',', ':')), each line ended by a newline including the last, and no blank line anywhere
retention_decisions_jsonl.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: a row carries these and no others, the same way additional_files_allowed settles the output directory
retention_decisions_jsonl.snapshot_id_note: snapshot_id is carried through as the plain string the source holds; the #RET-7101 coercions do not name it and it is not whitespace-collapsed

retention_state_json.container: object keyed by normalized repo, each value an object with the keys below

field_notes.daily/weekly/monthly/yearly/pinned: the snapshot ids the repo keeps in that role, ascending
field_notes.kept_count: how many snapshots the repo keeps in total
field_notes.quota_used: the GREATEST used_quota among the repo's kept snapshots -- the high-water mark the ledger reached over what survived, not a sum and not the value at the last one

retention_state_json.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: a row carries these and no others, the same way additional_files_allowed settles the output directory
retention_state_json.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline; the outer object is keyed by repo in ascending order and each repo's object carries its keys in the order required_fields lists them, which is not alphabetical

field_notes.canonical_snapshot_count: records that survive canonicalisation and deduplication, so one row per decision
field_notes.decision_counts: the per-kind counts again, keyed by decision
field_notes.max_overlap_count: the greatest overlap_count on any decision
field_notes.max_peak_depth: the greatest peak_depth on any decision
field_notes.max_quota_used: the greatest used_quota among all kept snapshots, over every repo
field_notes.raw_snapshot_count: records read from the inventory before canonicalisation
field_notes.selected_bucket_count: how many role slots the repos fill across daily, weekly, monthly and yearly, counted per snapshot per role, so one snapshot filling two roles counts twice
field_notes.total_size_bytes/kept_size_bytes/reclaim: stored bytes over all decisions, over the kept, over the pruned and over the deferred
field_notes.unique_snapshot_ids: distinct snapshot ids among the records read from the inventory, compared as the plain source strings they are: two ids differing only in their spacing are two ids, since the #RET-7101 coercions do not name snapshot_id

summary_json.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: a row carries these and no others, the same way additional_files_allowed settles the output directory
summary_json.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline; the object carries its keys in the order required_fields lists them and decision_counts carries its own in decision_counts_key_order, so neither is sorted alphabetically
